methodologyNotes: Specs sourced from manufacturer product pages (radpowerbikes.com, aventon.com, lectricebikes.com, ride1up.com) and reputable review aggregators (electricbikereview.com). Manufacturer pages for Specialized and Trek blocked 403/404 for direct scraping; electricbikereview.com served as primary source for those brands. priceUsd = US MSRP or starting price for the base/reference config (note: sale prices excluded where MSRP is documented). motor_w = nominal/rated wattage (not peak). range_mi = manufacturer claimed max or real-world tested depending on source; see provenance. weight_lb = total weight with battery unless noted. class = US e-bike class (1/2/3). throttle = true if any throttle mode available. release = model year or year launched. RadCity 5 Plus was discontinued ca. 2022; replaced in lineup by Radster Road (2024). Trek FX+ 2 was discontinued; current FX+ lineup is the FX+ 1S (2025). Soltera 2.5 is the current Soltera model (2024). Aventure.3 HS is the current Aventure (2025). A null beats any guess. All sources accessed 2026-06-15.

products.priceNote: US MSRP $1,499 for the High-Step base config (standard 720Wh battery). lectricebikes.com product page displays "$1,499" / "$1,499.00" (with a flash-sale compare-at of $1,835); electricbikereview.com lists "Price MSRP: $1,499". products.provenance: The lectricebikes.com XPeak2 High-Step product page confirms verbatim: a 750W rear hub motor (1310W peak, 85Nm torque), 28 mph top speed, "Class 1, 2, or 3 eBike", "up to 60 miles" range, a 48V 15Ah (720Wh) UL-2271 lithium battery, a thumb throttle alongside 5-level PAS, and a displayed price of $1,499 (flash-sale compare-at $1,835). That page also states the bike is "64.5 lbs w/o battery" and "The battery weighs 10.5 lbs," giving 75 lbs total-with-battery per the dataset's methodology (same total-with-battery convention used for the XP4 750W entry). electricbikereview.com's XPeak 2.0 review independently corroborates every figure in its spec table — "Price MSRP: $1,499", Motor Nominal Output 750W / Peak 1310W, Top Speed 28 mph, Electric Bike Class 3, 48V 15Ah 720Wh, Advertised Weight 64.5 lbs plus Battery Weight 10.5 lbs, and "Estimated Range (from Lectric): Up to 60 miles". Base/reference config is the standard 720Wh battery (the optional 960Wh upgrade is excluded); release year 2024 is confirmed by EBR's spec table "Availability: 2024" and "Model Year: 2024" (and EBR noting the 1.0 "launched just one year ago"). Corroboration is a review aggregator rather than a third-party retailer because Lectric sells direct-to-consumer only. Adversarial re-fetch (2026-07-10) of both URLs confirmed all eight spec values, priceUsd, and releaseDate verbatim; exact model verified as the XPeak 2.0 High-Step standard-battery config with no variant/capacity mismatch.
